hits.body:
Fixes four places where `cheme process reactor-hazards` understated the MTSR (`src/chemeascode/domains/safety/reaction_hazards.py`).

## Fixes

- **#303, gas batch at constant volume.** A gas-phase batch is always closed: the model refuses a vent or dosing without liquid-phase reactions. The batch model runs it at constant volume, with capacity `cp - R` and heat `dH - dnu R T`. The screening used `cp` and `dH`. `_heats` now takes `closed`, and `screen_node` passes it for `reactor: batch`. The same applies to the per-reaction rises and to the network potential (`_batch_network`). In the issue's case, dT_ad now equals the model's adiabatic run: 4810.9 K instead of 3436.4 K.
- **#304, isothermal batch T_p.** An isothermal batch is now screened at the temperature the model holds it at. That is its outlet's given or assumed temperature (`stirred_tank.outlet_temperature`, the lookup `solve_node` uses). Before, the screening used the charge temperature. An adiabatic batch still starts from the charge temperature.
- **#305, conversion, equilibrium and gibbs steps with a hotter outlet.** This fix differs from the issue's proposal, which was `T_p = T_out` with `X_ac = 1`. That proposal counts the converted share's heat twice in an adiabatic reactor. On the library it gave, for example, acetylene-1 R101 MTSR 3976 K and sulfuric-acid-1 R201 1225 K for an adiabatic converter bed whose MTSR is its 1029 K adiabatic outlet. Instead the step is screened from whichever of two states gives the larger MTSR:
  - the fresh feed at the inlet (`T_in + dT_ad`);
  - the outlet's state: its unconverted reactants at its temperature (`T_out + X_ac,r dT_ad,r`, where each reaction's `X_ac` comes from the outlets' composition).

  For an adiabatic step the two states agree. A heated step is screened from the outlet's state. Without the outlets' composition, the outlet's state is the fresh feed at `T_out`, which errs on the safe side and is what the issue asks for. A plug-flow bed stays at its inlet temperature, because `fixed_bed` starts there and an isothermal bed keeps it. The module docstring now states this rule.
- **#306, CSTR accumulation per reaction.** Each reaction now takes its own accumulation: the extent its limiting reactant still allows in the first tank, divided by the feed's. Before, the code used the first reactant of the first reaction for all of them. The MTSR is the largest `T_p + X_ac,r dT_ad,r` over the counted reactions, and the reported `X_ac` belongs to the reaction that sets it. Each reaction's own MTSR uses its own `X_ac`. Where no counted reaction is exothermic (the MTSR is `T_p`), the reported `X_ac` is the largest accumulation of a counted reaction, not the 0 of one whose reactants the feed lacks (a 0 K rise).

## Tests

`tests/test_reaction_hazards.py` gets one discriminating test per fix. All of them fail on `origin/main` and pass here:

- gas batch against the model's adiabatic run, and `dnu != 0`;
- isothermal and adiabatic batch with a given outlet;
- conversion step with outlet hotter, colder and absent, and with the outlet's composition (cooled, adiabatic, heated);
- two-reaction CSTR, with and without `hazard.reactions`;
- an endothermic conversion step with a second reaction the feed cannot run: the reported `X_ac` is the outlet's unconverted share (fails on this PR's earlier head 42d3cb6, which reported 0).

Docs: the reactions skill text is updated, `skills-manifest.json` regenerated, and `tests/data/init-manifest.txt` regenerated for the new `reactions/SKILL.md` hash (`test_init_golden`).

## Library effect

`process-library` origin/main (git archive), `cheme process reactor-hazards --json` on every entry, this branch against the pin (v1.12.0 + #254). 68 plants were screened; 40 entries have no `plant.yaml`. No criticality class or finding changes. No batch or CSTR entry changed.

| ammonia-1 | R501 (equilibrium) | 493.8 -> 703.2 | 670.1 -> 671.1 | 1 -> 0.70 | 1163.9 -> 1171.7 |

## Process-triggered gap
`separations/coverage.py` identifies liquid-liquid extraction as a specified component split, not an LLE unit. The phase module has liquid-phase capability, so the missing scope is its validated unit-operation/backend integration, not an assertion that all LLE thermodynamics is absent.

Source audit of core main `cec7e819e47c58ab036dcdcd4aec24810f08474a` (27 October 2026); source/docs inspected, no fresh solver run or blanket validation claim.

- `src/chemeascode/domains/process/separations/coverage.py`
- `src/chemeascode/domains/process/thermodynamics/phase.py`
- `src/chemeascode/domains/process/simulation/schema.py`

## Affected process-library work
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/170
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/185
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/186

These are **conditional prerequisites for the scoped predictive model/engineering claim**, not blockers to references, a brief, BFD or an explicitly sourced empirical inventory. Select route and target first.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] Choose an actual extraction route before requiring this adapter; some product routes can use other separations.
- [ ] Integrate a bounded equilibrium extraction stage/cascade using existing phase/property services or an established backend, with solvent and interaction-parameter provenance.
- [ ] Benchmark distribution/selectivity, phases, recovery, solvent loss and material/energy closure where evaluable, including failure for no two-phase region.
- [ ] Distinguish predictive extraction from specified splits and separate solvent regeneration from the extraction unit boundary.
- [ ] Add one reproducible positive reference test and meaningful unsupported/failure cases; record solver/data versions, tolerances and independent comparison.
- [ ] Update capability/maturity reporting, docs and the ADR for any public contract change; preserve existing ASU workflows.
- [ ] Link the evidence back to affected library issues and state which target is now supported.

## Coordination
Focused follow-up under #9 and #11; distinguish this implementation/qualification scope from general readiness #27. Reuse existing models and adapters rather than adding equations to skills or library folders. Library discovery trackers: ChemE-as-Code/process-library#306 and ChemE-as-Code/process-library#174.


---
_Comment (2026-10-27):_

Implementation in an earlier PR (`cheme process extract`, ADR 0019). Open gaps: (1) choosing an extraction route is up to the library; none of process-library#170/#185/#186 has selected one. (2) The one qualified system, water + 1-propanol + n-butyl acetate at 323.15 K, is benchmarked against tie lines that its 1-propanol NRTL pairs were partly fitted to. No freely accessible independent data set was found, so this qualifies the correlation as evaluated, not a blind prediction. (3) No energy balance (isothermal; tie-line NRTL does not qualify heats of mixing). (4) Solvent loss is over-predicted (qualified to 0.003 mole fraction absolute).

---
_Comment (2026-10-27):_

Merged in an earlier PR (squash bec7fe3) after an independent review. ADR 0019 records the decision.

**Now supported**
- `cheme process extract` reads `process/extraction.yaml` (`cheme/extraction/v1`). It solves countercurrent liquid-liquid equilibrium stages at one temperature on thermo's NRTL, with either a bundled LLE system or `model:` parameters that carry their source.
- It reports:
  - raffinate and extract
  - per-stage compositions
  - solute recovery and solvent loss
  - distribution coefficient (mass and mole basis) and selectivity
  - component closure (1e-8)
  - `split_to_extract`, for a flowsheet component separator's `basis_source`
  - model, backend and core versions, the parameter source, and the input fingerprints
- `energy: not-evaluated`, with the reason.
- Refusals, each a finding with file, line, rule and hint:
  - no two-phase region (`cheme.extraction-one-liquid`)
  - a missing NRTL pair (never taken as zero)
  - a temperature outside the parameters' range
  - an unknown component or system
  - a schema error
- The flowsheet keeps a specified `component_separator`, so maturity is unchanged. Solvent regeneration is a separate unit.

**Evidence (checked in the review)**
- **NRTL parameters**: Hajjar & Enders, Fluid Phase Equilib. 582 (2024) 114104, Tables 6 and 7 and Eq. (5). I verified them against the KITopen PDF.
- **Tie lines**: Costa et al., J. Chem. Eng. Data 54 (2009) 2845, 323.15 K, from NIST ThermoML je900337a data set 27. I verified them by parsing the file.
- **Benchmark** (`tests/test_extraction.py::test_the_bundled_system_reproduces_the_measured_tie_lines`), as tolerance (worst observed):

  | Quantity | Tolerance | Worst observed |
  |---|---|---|
  | Phase composition | 0.035 mole fraction | 0.029 |
  | 1-propanol distribution coefficient | 10 % | 8.3 % |
  | Selectivity | 15 % | 6.8 % |
  | n-butyl acetate in the aqueous phase | 0.003 abs | 0.0023 |

- Cascade tests check per-stage iso-activity (< 1e-7) and balance. As an independent algorithm check, the liquid split matches thermo's FlashVLN (water + ethyl acetate) to 1e-5.
- **Review fixes**:
  - A failed split of an unstable mixture used to be reported as a converged single liquid, which showed up as a false "no two-phase region" refusal. It is now reported as not converged, with a regression test.
  - The README placement is corrected.

**Remaining gaps (issue stays open)**
- [ ] Choosing an actual extraction route is up to the library. process-library#170, #185 and #186 have not selected one yet.
- The only qualified system is benchmarked against tie lines its 1-propanol pairs were partly fitted to. That qualifies the correlation as core evaluates it, not as a blind prediction. An independent data set, or a qualified system relevant to a library route, is still open.
- No energy balance (isothermal stages). Solvent loss is over-predicted 2 to 8 times, and qualified only to 0.003 mole fraction absolute. NRTL only; no stage efficiency or hydrodynamics.

Tracking issue: what the LCA and LCI machinery in core must do before the process library grows beyond ASU-1.

## Why now

Every LCI-contract change after processes are added (process-library `coverage.yaml`, `next: true`) means regenerating every process, so the contract and the checks should be stable first.

The ASU-1 footprint labels itself a **partial screening carbon footprint**:
- climate change only;
- 18 exchanges with gaps;
- ESTIMATE/PROXY factors;
- `process.yaml` states the characterisation factors are placeholders.

## Requirements (core side)

1. **Full impact assessment, not climate only.** Support one complete LCIA method (EF 3.1 recommended, for the EU PEF context; ReCiPe 2016 as an alternative) through the Brightway backend, with real EF 3.1 flow ids. See #26.
2. **No placeholder factors in published results.** Results computed with example or placeholder factors carry a status that fails `--strict` and the public build. Today the Atlas withholds them in public mode. Make this a core-level contract: `cheme assess lca` reports `factor_status` per exchange, and a `kind: lca` gate can require `published`.
3. **Balance gates on LCI datasets.** Mass, element and energy balances with fossil and biogenic carbon (#16), so that an LCI is never less consistent than the flowsheet it comes from.
4. **Completeness of emissions outside the stream table.** Combustion, fugitive, storage, flare and effluent estimates (#17). This is needed for the first reactive process (ammonia).
5. **Wastes, by-products and end of life** consistent with the system model (#18).
6. **Tiered LCIs** for processes without a full design, clearly labelled with the tier (#19).
7. **Regional scenarios** harmonised so that ASU results are comparable between regions (#25).
8. **Mapping workflow, provider profiles and double counting** (#14).
9. **Uncertainty.** Check the pedigree and uncertainty values (#26). The Monte Carlo interval is reported in the Atlas, so the inputs must be defensible.

## Done when

- [ ] ASU-1 has a full-LCIA result with no placeholder factors, and the result passes `--strict`.
- [ ] The LCI contract (dataset v2) is frozen and versioned, so new processes need no regeneration.
- [ ] The core docs (`docs/framework/lca.md`, `lci-scenarios.md`) state the scope and the limits.

Related: ChemE-as-Code/process-library#77, #78, #50, #51 and ChemE-as-Code/process-library#303 (mappings and system model).

---
_Status (2026-10-27):_

Requirement 2 (no placeholder factors in published results) is in place on the core side. #16 and #17 also received review fixes. The issue stays open because none of its "Done when" items is met yet.

**Done**
- Every exchange now gets a factor status: `gap`, `example`, `ASSUMED`, `PROXY`, `ESTIMATE`, `EPD`, `PUBLISHED`, `database` or `none`.
- The status is in `--json` and in `lca/manifest.json` (`result.factor_status`, `result.factors_published`).
- `cheme assess lca --strict` exits 1 when an exchange rests on an unpublished factor, and names it as `cheme.lca-factor-status`.
- New gate requirement `factors-published` for `kind: lca`. It is named this way so it cannot be confused with `publishable`.
- Fixes to the LCI balance gates from a review (requirement 3, #16).
- Fixes to the emission estimates from a review (requirement 4, #17). This includes fired reformers now being recognised as combustion units.

**Still open, and why**
- **Full LCIA (EF 3.1 or ReCiPe 2016).**
  - The method and its version still have to be chosen.
  - The EF 3.1 flow ids need the official package. `eplca.jrc.ec.europa.eu` was not reachable from the environment used. `scripts/fill_ef31_uuids.py` (#26) is ready for a downloaded copy.
- **Freezing dataset v2: deliberately not done.**
  - #18, #19 and #26 are open and can still change the contract.
  - Freezing now would cause the regeneration this issue is meant to avoid.
  - Proposal: freeze, with a schema snapshot test, once those three are closed.
- **ASU-1 full LCIA passing `--strict`.**
  - This needs ChemE-as-Code/process-library#303 (verified background mappings, final system model) plus real factors.
  - The library can now require `factors-published` in ASU-1's `checks.yaml` and run `--strict` in its public build.
- **Docs.**
  - `docs/framework/lca.md` now states the factor-status contract.
  - The scope and limits text should be written once the method is chosen.
- **Requirements 5 to 9** (#18, #19, #25, #14, #26) were not part of this round.

No factors and no data were invented. EPA, EEA and JRC sources were blocked by the network policy of that environment.

## Goal

Develop ChemE-as-Code toward coordinated detailed engineering, extending existing preliminary sizing into reproducible equipment design, rating and qualified discipline checks. These calculations underpin the coordinated design-change demonstration (#216), constrained improvement (#218) and brownfield retrofit (#219).

**Priority: P1-high.** First delivery: integrated control-valve, pipe and pump calculations; next: exchanger rating and column hydraulics. Remaining capabilities are high-priority backlog work, sequenced after these foundations rather than implemented simultaneously.

## Scope

Create focused implementation issues for:
1. Control-valve sizing and candidate rating.
2. Pipe diameter selection and network hydraulics.
3. Pump curve selection and operating-point checks.
4. Heat-exchanger thermal and hydraulic rating.
5. Tray and packed-column hydraulic sizing.
6. Scenario-specific relief loads and device sizing.
7. Separator and knockout-drum sizing.
8. Compressor-map evaluation.
9. Utility-system sizing and capacity checks.
10. Preliminary mechanical checks and equipment weights.

Reuse existing sizing, hydraulics, thermodynamics, datasheet, provenance and spatial contracts. Related broad capability audit: #9; historical backlog #8 is closed and is context only.

## Shared implementation requirements

- Typed, unit-aware deterministic calculations in the owning core domains; CLI and agent instructions wrap the same functions.
- Inspect current code/tests before implementation and extend rather than replace working calculations.
- Methods, input sources, validity ranges, optional dependency versions and model assumptions recorded with each result.
- Independent numerical benchmarks, physical invariants, invalid-input and unsupported-regime tests with declared tolerances.
- Versioned inputs, stable equipment/line/stream IDs, operating cases, calculation records and staleness fingerprints.
- Reuse established libraries via thin adapters where appropriate, after checking API, license and supported regimes.
- Keep supplied manufacturer data distinct from estimates; missing curves, coefficients or properties must remain explicit.
- Update sizing coverage, schemas, documentation and skills to reflect actual demonstrated maturity.
- No claim of mechanical-code compliance or manufacturer selection solely from preliminary calculations.

## Integrated acceptance demonstration

A 20% throughput increase reveals a real hydraulic constraint. Compare valve trim/size, pipe diameter and pump options using a coupled pressure balance. Show feasible operating points at minimum/normal/maximum demand, update datasheets and engineering diffs, and propagate supported economic consequences.

## Implementation issues

- [ ] #221 — Control valves: liquid/gas sizing and candidate rating across operating cases
- [ ] #222 — Piping: diameter selection and coupled hydraulic network solution
- [ ] #223 — Pumps: curve-based selection, system operating points and NPSH checks
- [ ] #224 — Heat exchangers: geometry-based thermal and hydraulic rating
- [ ] #225 — Columns: tray and packing hydraulic sizing, flooding and turndown
- [ ] #226 — Relief: supported scenario loads, device sizing and discharge pressure-loss checks
- [ ] #227 — Separators: gas–liquid and knockout-drum process sizing
- [ ] #228 — Compressors: supplied-map operating points and surge/choke margins
- [ ] #229 — Utilities: cooling-water, steam and compressed-air network sizing and capacity checks
- [ ] #230 — Mechanical screening: pressure thickness checks and equipment weight estimates

## Delivery sequence

1. #221 + #222 + #223: integrated valve–pipe–pump package and a throughput-change benchmark.
2. #224 + #225: exchanger rating and column hydraulics.
3. #226: staged relief capability with specialist method review.
4. #227–#230: separator, compressor-map, utility and mechanical extensions, driven by representative library cases.

All children are P1-high. This sequence expresses implementation dependencies and focus; it is not a claim they can all be completed in parallel.


## Detailed engineering is the explicit platform target

The intended destination is detailed engineering, including qualified discipline calculations, equipment selection/rating, coordinated drawings and schedules, supplier-data integration and an auditable review/issue workflow. Preliminary calculations and demonstrations are intermediate milestones.

Track capability per equipment/service/method and discipline rather than assigning a single blanket maturity to an entire plant. Distinguish:
1. Preliminary sizing with stated assumptions.
2. Independently benchmarked process design and existing-equipment rating.
3. Qualified discipline checks for a declared standard/edition and supported load/service envelope.
4. Coordinated detailed engineering package with supplier data, resolved interfaces and documented review/sign-off.

A calculation library alone does not complete levels 3–4. Define each deliverable's required inputs/checks, unresolved items and review evidence.

## Additional high-priority capability issues

- [ ] #231 — Thermal design: insulation, heat loss, condensation protection and heat tracing
- [ ] #232 — Heat pumps and refrigeration: cycle design, equipment duties and off-design rating
- [ ] #233 — Vacuum systems: evacuation dynamics, process loads, condensers and pump rating
- [ ] #234 — Agitation and mixing: power, torque, impeller sizing and process performance
- [ ] #235 — Solid–liquid separation: filtration and centrifugation equipment sizing and cycle rating
- [ ] #236 — Drying: kinetic models, equipment sizing and coupled heat/mass-transfer rating
- [ ] #237 — Materials engineering: compatibility evidence, corrosion screening and selection records
- [ ] #238 — Piping mechanics: thermal expansion, flexibility screening and qualified stress-analysis integration
- [ ] #239 — Hydraulic transients: valve closure, pump trips and surge-protection studies
- [ ] #240 — Electrical engineering: load lists, motor/drive sizing, cables and protection checks

Drying work reuses #144 and #183; it does not replace their benchmark and model follow-ups.

## Cross-discipline detailed-engineering milestones

- [ ] Maintain a machine-readable capability/verification matrix by calculation, equipment, service, load case and code/edition, linking evidence and unresolved checks.
- [ ] Define required deliverables and completeness gates for process, piping, mechanical, instrumentation/control, electrical and structural interfaces.
- [ ] Support supplier data ingestion and revision handling: curves, certified dimensions, connection loads, materials, operating limits and actual device selections.
- [ ] Make both new-design sizing and existing-equipment rating first-class workflows; identify limiting operating cases and constraints.
- [ ] Connect piping classes/specifications, pressure/temperature ratings, wall/schedule selection, supports, flexibility/stress results and nozzle-load interfaces.
- [ ] Audit and plan the remaining drawing/schedule deliverables: fabrication/installation isometrics with dimensions and bills of materials, instrument datasheets/hook-ups/I/O and loop records, electrical single-line/cable/protection outputs, foundations/support loads and discipline interfaces.
- [ ] Extend current sign-off/gate mechanisms to calculation checking, discipline/interface review, unresolved deviations, issue status and complete revision/change propagation.
- [ ] Deliver a full industrial process-plant reference package under #253, spanning process units, utilities/offsites and discipline interfaces. Qualify individual methods on small fixtures, but measure programme acceptance against the complete plant-wide deliverable/check matrix.

## Sequencing of the expanded scope

Preserve #221–#225 as the first connected engineering foundation. Add insulation/tracing (#231), cycles (#232), vacuum (#233) and mixing (#234) next as case d

## Goal
Expose the existing core reactor-profile calculations in the current viewer, with a clear view of peak temperature, its location and optional user-defined temperature limits. Use an existing process/reactor detail view or a dedicated tab inside the viewer; no separate app/repository.

## Existing basis and integration
Core's `domains/process/fixed_bed.py` returns outlet quantities, a temperature/pressure profile along catalyst mass, and a peak-temperature value. Its current model is steady-state, ideal-gas and pseudo-homogeneous, with effective particle rates, adiabatic/isothermal/cooled modes and optional pressure drop.
Inspect the current reactor report/API before adding endpoints. Reuse viewer process/simulation components and core's read-only API/snapshot conventions.
Future optional backend: #12
The viewer must work with today's computation; it must not depend on IDAES.

## Profile display
- [ ] Select a reactor and operating case, linked to its process object/equipment where available.
- [ ] Plot temperature and pressure against the actual coordinate returned by core: catalyst mass in kg initially. Show units and distinguish inlet/outlet.
- [ ] Do not label catalyst mass as axial length. Offer length/normalized coordinate only when a documented, validated conversion is available.
- [ ] Show inlet/outlet temperature, peak temperature, temperature rise, pressure drop, catalyst mass and calculation mode.
- [ ] Show conversion/composition profiles only if actually returned; do not invent internal compositions from endpoint values.
- [ ] Support usable legends, tooltips, accessible colors and a tabular view/download where appropriate.
- [ ] Support both local live API and exported snapshots with a shared versioned result shape.

## Hotspot screening
- [ ] Mark the maximum and its coordinate, explicitly distinguishing an interior hotspot from an endpoint maximum.
- [ ] Show optional user-supplied allowable temperature limits as annotated reference lines with source/basis and provenance.
- [ ] Report peak-minus-limit and intervals exceeding the limit where a limit exists; without one, report the peak without a safe/unsafe judgement.
- [ ] Distinguish coolant temperature, catalyst operating-range guidance and an engineering maximum allowable temperature; they are not interchangeable.
- [ ] If the existing result contains a peak value but no location, extend the core result contract minimally. Do not mislocate an internal integration-step peak using the nearest sampled display point.
- [ ] Distinguish sampled maximum from solver-tracked peak; expose profile resolution and peak-location precision. Require refinement checks where coarse sampling could miss a narrow hotspot.
- [ ] Keep extrema/threshold calculations in shared core result/report logic, not duplicated scientific algorithms in the browser.

## Calculation and validity states
- [ ] Display source revision, input fingerprint, tool/model version and operating case.
- [ ] Show missing kinetics/properties, failure/non-convergence, stale inputs and uncomputed results explicitly.
- [ ] Show assumptions and diagnostics, including omitted pressure drop when geometry/viscosity is missing.
- [ ] An axial steady-state temperature maximum is screening information, not a dynamic runaway, thermal-stability or particle-scale hotspot analysis.
- [ ] Do not imply radial or intraparticle temperatures are resolved by the current pseudo-homogeneous model.
- [ ] The viewer reads results; it does not write plant files or run hidden calculations on page load.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A real existing core reactor example renders its T/P profiles and endpoint/peak values.
- [ ] Fixtures cover monotonic and interior-peak profiles, isothermal operation, threshold exceedance, no limit, missing data, stale results and failures.
- [ ] Values, coordinate units and peak location agree with the core result, including distinction between sampled and solver peaks.
- [ ] A declared limit shows an accurate exceedance summary; absence of a limit produces no invented approval.
- [ ] API and snapshot views convey the same results/status/assumptions.
- [ ] Existing process and simulation views remain usable; no IDAES installation is required.

## Suggested implementation
1. Audit existing core report/API profile output and agree the minimal shared result fields.
2. Add read-only result exposure/snapshot inclusion in core if required.
3. Implement charts, peak/limit summary and validity states in viewer.
4. Verify against an existing reactor example and focused fixtures.


---
_Comment (2026-10-24):_

## Optional per-process data and conditional UI
Reactor-profile calculations are not required for every process/library entry. Absence of profile data is normal and must not lower unrelated maturity checks or create empty pages.

- [ ] Discover available reactor result artifacts/capabilities per process, reactor and operating case.
- [ ] Hide the reactor-profile tab/section when no result or explicit run record exists. Do not show empty charts, zero placeholders or a mandatory empty reactor page.
- [ ] Show only the quantities actually available: temperature-only data must not create an empty pressure/composition panel.
- [ ] If a known calculation is failed, pending or stale, show that meaningful status and diagnostic rather than treating it as absent or hiding the failure. Stale historical curves must be clearly labelled.
- [ ] A hotspot summary requires suitable temperature-profile/peak data; threshold-exceedance UI additionally requires an explicit limit.
- [ ] No automatic solver execution or fabricated/default data to populate the view.
- [ ] Test a process with no reactors, a reactor without profile computation, partial profile data, valid results and failed/stale run records.
This conditional-display principle should also guide other optional analysis views: present available evidence and meaningful execution states, without manufacturing empty pages.

---
_Comment (2026-10-27):_

An earlier viewer PR is merged. Each `reactor: pfr` now has a fixed-bed card on the Reactions page. It works against `cheme serve` and against static snapshots: `/api/reactions` per case, plus `/api/simulation` only when the page has a bed.

- **Reference lines:** the coolant temperature (a boundary condition) and the catalyst window (operating guidance), each labelled with its basis and provenance. Neither is treated as a limit. With no engineering limit served, the peak is reported without a safe or unsafe judgement.
- **Reading the data:** a crosshair readout by hover or keyboard, a legend, the profile table and CSV.
- **Notes and missing data:** core's notes (e.g. no pressure drop and why). A constant T or P profile is described in words instead of drawn.
- **Run record:** the bed's row of the recorded simulation run, shown as current, stale (changed files listed, values marked historical), staleness unknown, or not converged. Errors reading the simulation are shown.

## Process-triggered gap
`thermodynamics/methods.yml:58–61` states petroleum pseudocomponents unsupported. Phase route needs identified compounds; DWSIM translation has no assay characterization input and expects database compounds.

Source audit of core main `cec7e819e47c58ab036dcdcd4aec24810f08474a` (27 October 2026); source/docs inspected, no fresh solver run or blanket validation claim.

- `src/chemeascode/domains/process/thermodynamics/methods.yml`
- `src/chemeascode/domains/process/simulation/schema.py`

## Affected process-library work
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/176
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/181

These are **conditional prerequisites for the scoped predictive model/engineering claim**, not blockers to references, a brief, BFD or an explicitly sourced empirical inventory. Select route and target first.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] Define sourced assay/cut descriptors and deterministic characterization, with versioned component identity and property provenance; use established backend characterization methods.
- [ ] Choose one bounded naphtha/fraction reference and validate mass basis, boiling/density behavior and flash/enthalpy results with justified tolerances.
- [ ] Include characterization in fingerprints, run records and comparability checks; reject insufficient assays and unsupported extrapolation.
- [ ] Preserve a pure-component ethane cracker/gas route as a separate scope that does not depend on this extension.
- [ ] Add one reproducible positive reference test and meaningful unsupported/failure cases; record solver/data versions, tolerances and independent comparison.
- [ ] Update capability/maturity reporting, docs and the ADR for any public contract change; preserve existing ASU workflows.
- [ ] Link the evidence back to affected library issues and state which target is now supported.

## Coordination
Focused follow-up under #9 and #11; distinguish this implementation/qualification scope from general readiness #27. Reuse existing models and adapters rather than adding equations to skills or library folders. Library discovery trackers: ChemE-as-Code/process-library#306 and ChemE-as-Code/process-library#174.


---
_Comment (2026-10-27):_

Merged in an earlier PR (squash 64a568e). Summary of what is now supported, the evidence and what remains.

**Supported**
- `process/assays.yaml` (`cheme/assay/v1`): sourced assays with a TBP or ASTM D86 curve plus SG/API/density/Watson K, or explicit cuts. `cheme process assay` characterises them deterministically into versioned pseudocomponents `pseudo:<fingerprint>:<n>`. The steps are API TDB 3A1.1 D86→TBP, equal-volume cuts, constant Watson K, Riazi-Daubert (1987) M/Tc/Pc/C-H, Lee-Kesler ω and Lastovka-Shaw Cp through `thermo`. Every property records the correlation that produced it.
- Refusals: `cheme.assay-insufficient` (also a D86 50 % point at or below 0 °F) and `cheme.assay-extrapolation` (outside `assay.RANGES`) produce no pseudocomponents. `--fill` writes `process/assay-characterization.json`, and `cheme validate`/`--check` report `cheme.assay-record-stale`/`-missing`. `assay.comparability()` compares two characterisations.
- A Peng-Robinson bubble/dew/flash is claimed only inside `assay.FLASH_CLAIM`: 300–550 K, 50–500 kPa(a), pseudocomponents of 340–448 K and SG 0.66–0.875. `methods.yml` `petroleum_pseudocomponents` gains `elsewhere: {assay: limited}`, and the phase and simulation routes stay `unsupported`. The decision is in ADR 0026, with docs in `docs/framework/assay.md`.

**Evidence** (`tests/test_assay.py`)
- Published assay: TotalEnergies OMAN crude assay (2020), heavy naphtha 80–175 °C. Pseudocomponent mass fractions match the assay's wt % curve within 0.015 (worst 0.010). The cross-predicted cut densities are 734.2 / 741.8 against the measured 734 / 742 kg/m³ (tolerance 2 kg/m³). The bubble and dew points are ordered within the TBP curve.
- Two defined naphtha surrogates checked against CoolProp 8.0.0 reference models (GERG-2008 / Bell et al. 2016): saturation T within 2.0 K (worst 1.79 K), enthalpy differences within 20 kJ/kg (worst 18.2), M within 3 % (worst 1.5 %), ρ15 within 1 % (worst 0.15 %).
- Correlations reproduce published worked examples (Riazi MNL50 Ex. 3.3, the API 3A1.1 example, Ahmed Ex. 2.2). In review, the coefficients and the OMAN data points were spot-checked against the sources.
- The ethane/gas route is independent: the phase and simulation modules do not import `assay`, and the phase route still refuses pseudocomponents.

**Remaining (why this issue stays open)**
- The flash/enthalpy part of the reference check rests on surrogates. No openly available measured flash/enthalpy data for a real naphtha was found.
- Pseudocomponents are not accepted by `simulation.yaml`/DWSIM, so simulation run records do not include the characterisation.
- Light ends ≤ C5 and fractions above 650 °F are refused (outside the fitted ranges).

A controller output that moves a compressor's inlet guide vanes (e.g. the low select UY-4151 to the K-4101 vanes, FIC-3107 to the K-4102 vanes) can only be drawn as a free PolyLine. There is no SignalLineFunction target and no actuating function / actuator object for the vanes, so:

- the lists-vs-P&ID checks and the HAZOP / loop cross-checks cannot verify the final element of the loop;
- `cheme fragment signal --to` has no target for it.

Wanted: a way to model the guide vanes (or any machine-internal final element: speed, stroke, vanes) as the target of a signal line, e.g. an ActuatingFunction / ActuatingSystem owned by the compressor, with a fragment and `show` support. The plant currently records the gap in DESIGN.md D-101.

hits.body:
## What happens

In `src/chemeascode/domains/process/model.py` (v1.13.0, b97a833), `_reactor_rules` binds

```python
declared = process.reactions.by_id() if process.reactions else {}   # line 972
```

and looks every block's and step's reactions up in it (`reactions = [declared[n] for n in item.reactions if n in declared]`, line 978). Inside the same loop, the `selectivity:` branch rebinds the name:

```python
declared = [r.id for r in reactions if r.conversion is not None]    # line 1098
```

From the first item with a `selectivity:` block on, `declared` is a list of ids. For every later block or step:

- if that list is empty (the usual case), `n in declared` is false for every reaction, so `reactions` is empty and the reactor rules of the later items (conversion lacking, equilibrium, pfr, selectivity key and products) run on no reactions and report nothing;
- if it is not empty, `declared[n]` indexes a list with a string and raises `TypeError`.

So only the first `selectivity:` reactor of a flowsheet is checked in full; the reactors after it are checked silently against no reactions.

## Expected

Each item is checked against the flowsheet's reactions. A different name for the list in the selectivity branch (e.g. `with_conversion`) fixes it.

## Where it was met

The process library records it in three entries, each of which worked around it: ibuprofen-1 (L-6, PR ChemE-as-Code/process-library#562: R201 written with reaction conversions so R301 keeps its selectivity), ethylene-glycol-1 and acetic-anhydride-1 (DESIGN.md, "To report to core").

hits.body:
Part of #165 (feature F3: NBS lessons L-2 and L-5).

## What it does

**The crystallizer accepts a mixed liquor** (`domains/process/crystallization.py`, `schema.py`)
- `crystallizer.spectators: [ids]` names other dissolved components (salts, base, unreacted reagent). They pass with the liquor unchanged: they never crystallize or evaporate. They divide between cake and filtrate with the liquid, and each has its own triple in the balances and atoms in the element balance.
- The solubility then has to hold in that liquor. There are two ways to give it:
  - `solubility.measured_in: mother_liquor`: data measured in that liquor. This adds a new unit, `kg/kg_liquor` (per kg of solute-free liquor), so that `C = (S - s (W + P)) / (a - s (1 - a))`. A `mass_fraction` measured in the liquor is `x / (1 - x)` on that basis.
  - `solubility.salting_out: {coefficients: {id: k}, log: log10|ln}`: a pure-solvent solubility with a Setschenow correction, `log10(s0/s) = sum k_i m_i` on the molal scale. Every spectator needs a coefficient (state 0 for one with no effect). With a hydrate the correction is solved by successive substitution on the free solvent.
- A pure-solvent value on its own is refused, never used silently:
  - `cheme.process-crystallizer` reports an error with file, line and hint;
  - `propagate` refuses the step as unsupported;
  - the model basis is reported as not sourced.
- An inlet component that is not declared is still refused, as before.

**A crystallizer can take several inlets.** They are taken together, and the energy balance uses their mass-weighted mean feed temperature. This makes a **reslurry wash** a crystallizer fed by the cake and the wash water: the crystals dissolve until the liquid is saturated, and its `separation:` or a following `solid_separation:` re-filters. No new `wash:` block was needed.

**Phase changes are no longer screened as reactions** (`chemistry/reactions.py`, `safety/reaction_hazards.py`)
- A reaction can now declare `kind: phase-change`.
- A reaction of one component into one other with the same formula, one of them `phase: solid`, counts as a phase change without the field. Isomerizations stay reactions.
- `cheme process reactor-hazards`:
  - skips a step whose reactions are all phase changes;
  - reports it as `cheme.reactor-hazard-phase-change` (info, stable id `process/flowsheet.yaml#reactor-hazard-phase-change:<step>`) and lists it under JSON `phase_changes`;
  - screens a step with both kinds on its chemical reactions alone.

**Fingerprints are unchanged.**
- Every new field uses `exclude_if` at its default. `kind` is also left out of `Reaction.inputs_dump`.
- The Felder 4.5-2 plant's outlet fingerprints are pinned to the values core 1.7.0 writes, for both `basis: solubility` and `basis: yield`.
- `cheme process crystallizers` adds the `mother_liquor` and `spectators` keys only when there are spectators.

**PharmaPy was reviewed and not adopted.** Assimulo cannot be installed with uv on Python 3.12+, and its crystallizers need population-balance kinetics with no electrolyte thermodynamics. The model here is native, and PharmaPy is cited in the ADR only as literature.

## Tests (`tests/test_precipitation.py`, checked against hand calculations)
- Mass balance with spectators, on both the per-kg-of-liquor and the per-kg-of-solvent basis, with element and spectator residuals.
- Mass fraction measured in the liquor.
- Interpolation of a solubility table measured in the liquor (no extrapolation).
- Setschenow correction against a hand calculation: s = 0.020 x 10^-0.15 = 0.0141589, C = 35.8411 kg/h. The `ln` form gives the same, and a hydrate solved by successive substitution is consistent.
- Spectators through a recycle and purge.
- Reslurry dissolution (1.5725 kg/h dissolve; a large excess of water leaves the liquor undersaturated).
- Schema refusals.
- An NBS-like flowsheet (precipitation, filter, reslurry crystallizer with two inlets) that propagates, balances and reports.
- A pure-water solubility in a mixed liquor is refused, and an undeclared solute is still refused.
- Phase-change detection (declared, same formula plus a solid, isomer not detected); the hazard screening skips the phase-change step and screens a mixed step on its reaction.
- Old crystallizers keep their 1.7.0 fingerprints.

`uv run pytest -n auto`: 4266 passed, 131 skipped. `ruff format` and `ruff check` are clean. `mkdocs build --strict` passes.

## Docs and regenerated files
- ADR 0056, with its row in `docs/adr/README.md` and an entry in `mkdocs.yml`.
- REFERENCE.md (crystallizer and reactive hazard screening).
- Skills `separation-method-selection` (including the coverage table and its note) and `reactions`.
- CHANGELOG under Unreleased.
- Regenerated: the skill manifest and init manifest; the example BFD/PFD sheets (the process schema changed); the `yaml-flowsheet.json` viewer fixture.

## Limits
- Data measured in the liquor hold at the composition their source states; the model does not check that the solved liquor is still at that composition.
- The Setschenow correction is the empirical molal-scale form. There is no electrolyte activity model, no solubility product and no check of a spectator's own solubility limit.
- One crystallizing solute only.
- A hydrate formation written as a reaction is detected as a phase change only when it declares `kind: phase-change`.
- The NBS library entry itself (CR101, W101) is re-expressed in the library, not here.

Closes #183 for what a model can decide: the crystallizer and dryer follow-ups of ADRs 0056/0057, plus the cases from the issue's comment. ADR 0072.

**Targets 1.13.0.** 1.12.0 is released and `integration/1.12.0` is in `main`, so this PR now targets `main`; `origin/main` (0e85885, #254) is merged in and the changelog entry sits under Unreleased.

## Done

Each item is optional. A flowsheet without the new fields solves, fingerprints and reports as before.

1. **One solubility point, carried with an explicit ASSUMED transfer** (NBS L-8, CBr4 L-4).
   - Usage: `solubility: {points: [[T0, s0]], transfer: {heat_of_solution: kJ/kmol, provenance, source}}`. This applies to pure-solvent data only.
   - Method: van 't Hoff for an ideal solution at a constant heat of solution, `ln(x/x0) = -(dH/R)(1/T - 1/T0)`, applied to the solute's mole fraction.
   - Reporting: `solubility_transfer` appears in `crystallizers --json`, an info `cheme.process-crystallizer-transfer` says "not a value at the operating conditions", and the model basis says the same and is unsourced while the transfer is assumed.
   - Without `transfer:`, the point is refused as before.
   - Check on a scratch copy of n-bromosuccinimide-1: replacing both `value: 0.0147` with the 298.15 K point and `heat_of_solution: 0` gives the same crystals (CR101 63.917 kg/h, W101 -1.4066 kg/h), now reported honestly.
2. **Liquor composition check** (NaN3 L-6).
   - Usage: `measured_in: mother_liquor` data may give `liquor: {mass_fraction: {spectator: w}, tolerance}`.
   - `crystallizers` compares the solved mother liquor with it (`mother_liquor.composition`) and warns beyond the tolerance (`cheme.process-crystallizer-liquor`).
3. **Washes** (NaN3 L-8).
   - Usage: `solid_separation.wash: {port, efficiency, cake_liquid, dissolution}`, a displacement wash on the filter with the wash by its own inlet.
   - Model: `R = (1 - E)^n` of the unwashed cake's liquor stays, where n is the mass wash ratio (the SysCAD filter-press mass-ratio form; that section cites no source, the page's Merritt reference belongs to its volume-ratio method). The washed cake holds its cake liquid, and the rest of that liquid is wash.
   - `dissolution:` dissolves crystals into the wash up to a stated approach to their solubility per kg of wash. This works in any wash liquid, e.g. NaN3 into aqueous methanol. It is balanced in `validate` as a phase change.
   - An optional `wash_filtrate` outlet keeps the wash filtrate separate.
   - A recipe `filter` adds the wash's time at the final filtration rate, `mu V_w (alpha M/A^2 + R_m/A)/dP`. `M` in Ruth's and the wash's time is the unwashed cake's solid. The recipe vessel holds the slurry or, later, the unwashed cake with the wash, the larger of the two, not their sum.
4. **Dryer** (NBS L-7).
   - `cooling: {product_temperature, heat_capacity, vessel_temperature, port}` covers the product cooled before discharge and the vessel cooled back for the next batch. The heating then starts from that vessel temperature.
   - `condenser: {temperature, heat_capacity, port}` is the vacuum condenser: a Rachford-Rice flash at the dryer's `pressure` over an ideal condensate. It gives a duty (the latent heat of what condenses plus all of the vapour cooled as liquid, the vent condenser's path) and an optional `condensate` outlet.
   - With `cooling:` or `condenser:`, propagate writes the outlets' temperatures.
   - The cooling and condenser duties are compared with their energy streams (`cheme.process-dryer-duty`).
5. **CBr4 L-5**:
   - `sublimation: {components: {solid: vapour}, heat}`: the vapour leaves saturated with the subliming solid at the dryer's pressure, which is an upper bound of the loss. Its heat goes into the duty, and it is balanced as a phase change.
   - `selectivity: raoult`: the volatiles kept are what an open (Rayleigh) evaporation of an ideal cake liquid leaves, `n_i = n_i0 f^(P_i/P_max)`. It is solved by bisection on the least volatile's share `f^(P_min/P_max)`, so a volatile 100 times less volatile than the main one still dries to the residual moisture; a split that misses it is refused.
6. **TsCl L-4 (the oil)**:
   - `solid_separation.second_liquid: {components, cake_liquid}`: the cake holds the oil at its own cake liquid.
   - `crystallizer.second_liquid: {components}`: these spectators are left out of a per-liquor solubility basis, the salting-out molality and the liquor check (`liquor.mass_fraction` refuses them). With no other spectator, a pure-solvent solubility (also a carried one) holds in the mother liquor.
7. **Model basis**: a filter is not sourced while its `wash`, the wash's `dissolution` and its solubility (and transfer) or its `second_liquid` is assumed; a dryer while its `sublimation`, `cooling` or `condenser` is; a crystallizer while its `second_liquid` is. The detail names them (`not sourced: ...`). A dryer with `cooling:` or `condenser:` states the outlet temperatures propagate writes.

## Left open, and why

- **The solute's share in a second liquid** (p-TsCl dissolved in the o-TsCl oil): a stream has one composition per component, so a following filter could not split the dissolved solute by phase. This needs a pseudo-component or phase-resolved streams.
- **A second crystallizing solute** (the ortho isomer as a solid): this is ternary solid-liquid equilibrium (a eutectic or solid solution). It needs phase-diagram data that no entry has, so the crystallizer stays one solute.
- **The wash efficiency itself**: a dispersion or channelling model of the cake needs porosity, dispersion and particle data that no entry has. E is specified.
- **Leaked air in the vacuum condenser, and the sublimate's deposit there**: no leak rate or deposition data are declared. The sublimate passes the condenser uncounted, with a note in the report.
- **A drying curve**: still no measured data (as in ADR 0057).

## Review fixes (round 5)

All 11 confirmed findings are fixed, each with a test that fails on the previous head:
- `kept_by` bisected on `f` and stopped at about 2^-201, so a heavy volatile kept far more than the residual moisture (2.42 % against 1 %). Now it bisects on the least volatile's share and refuses a miss (`test_selective_drying_of_a_volatile_far_less_volatile_than_the_main_one`).
- Model basis: the wash, dissolution, second liquid, sublimation, cooling and condenser now count for `sourced`. The dryer basis no longer says that the product and vapour leave at the drying temperature when propagate writes other temperatures.
- A `liquor.mass_fraction` of a second-liquid component is refused.
- A crystallizer whose only spectators form the second liquid takes a pure-solvent or carried solubility. Before, it was refused with a hint the schema could not accept.
- Recipe filter time and vessel of a washed filter: see item 3 above.
- The condenser duty text in the schema, REFERENCE and ADR now matches the code. A partial-condensation test pins it.
- ADR 0072 now records the SysCAD/Merritt source correctly.
- The branch is up to date with `main`. The examples are rebuilt and only `generator_sha256` changed.

## Library effect

None intended, and none found.

- Entries checked: the ten entries with a crystallizer, filter or dryer, from a fresh `git archive origin/main` of the process library. The library's pin CLI (core 0e85885) was run against this branch's CLI, with JSON compared numerically at rel 1e-9 and text exactly. The entries: carbon-tetrabromide-1, copper-i-chloride-1, dmf-1, methylmagnesium-bromide-1, methyltriphenylphosphonium-bromide-1, n-bromosuccinimide-1, p-toluenesulfonyl-chloride-1, potassium-tert-butoxide-1, sodium-azide-1, tert-butyldimethylsilyl-chloride-1.
- Commands: `process propagate --check`, and `--json` of `process streams`, `recipe`, `reactors`, `reactor-hazards`, `stills` and `crystallizers`, with their exit codes.
- Result: identical for all ten entries (outputs and exit codes), with no differences at rel 1e-9 and none in the text.

## Problem
A safeguard referencing an instrument or interlock does not establish that the complete protection function acts on the equipment and scenario claimed. Candidate discovery must be followed by explicit chain verification.

## Scope
Implementation slice of #249, building on the scenario-specific claim/check contract in #261 and configuration handling in #262. Extend existing control-loop, cause-and-effect, plant-reference and DEXPI contracts; do not create a duplicate control model.

- Resolve the claimed protection function from sensor/measurement through logic or interlock to the final element and affected process equipment.
- Check the measured variable, initiating condition, trip direction/action, final-element identity and intended process effect against the specific claim.
- Trace signal relationships separately from physical process connectivity; distinguish a complete trip function from an alarm requiring operator action.
- Identify missing links, conflicting references, bypass/inhibit conditions and unsupported logic. Keep configuration and evidence revisions explicit.
- Use deterministic checks where structured evidence supports them. Missing response-time, setpoint or process-effect evidence remains unresolved rather than being inferred from tags.
- Preserve proposed/accepted human judgement separately from automated check results.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Valid sensor → logic → actuator chains return resolvable evidence for each link and the protected-equipment reference.
- [ ] Fixtures detect a wrong measured variable, wrong final element, reversed trip action, missing signal link and bypassed/inhibited function.
- [ ] An alarm with no evidenced operator-response provision cannot pass as an automatic trip.
- [ ] Complete connectivity does not imply adequate response time, SIL, independence or risk-reduction credit.
- [ ] Unsupported logic and missing evidence produce scoped insufficient-evidence results.
- [ ] Expose results through existing safety CLI/API and reports; fingerprint dependencies for #263.

A project can now declare a line or segment as **buried** in `piping/routing.yaml`. The headroom rule then leaves the buried runs alone, and a new cover rule checks them instead. ADR 0036.

```yaml
lines:
  - {line: CWS-1144, segment: P-114/Line_CWS1144_S2, route: [...], buried: {basis: D-038}}
  - {line: CWS-1041, elevation: -1.8, buried: {cover_m: 1.0, basis: D-038}}
```

## Acceptance checks

| Check | Done |
|---|---|
| A project can declare a line, segment or route part as buried in `piping/routing.yaml` | `LineRouting.buried`: `true` or `{cover_m?, basis?}`, for a line or one segment, like the other intent. The schema refuses `buried` with `rack`/`tier` or with an `elevation` ≥ 0, and a `cover_m` ≤ 0. Schema errors carry the file and line, as before. The **route part** is the geometry: a run of a buried pipe counts as buried where its top (axis + OD/2 + insulation) is at or below grade (z = 0). Risers and runs at grade stay above-grade pipes. The router copies the declaration onto the model pipe (`buried`, optional). `cheme layout pin` keeps it (`ROUTE_KEEPS`). |
| 1. The headroom rule does not apply to buried parts | Buried samples are skipped by the road headroom rule, and buried runs by the escape-route headroom. A run at grade over a road is **still** a `layout-headroom` finding (tested). |
| 1. A buried route under a road needs at least its cover; new finding; minimum ASSUMED, configurable and documented | New `cheme.layout-buried-cover` (warning). It fires when the cover over the pipe top is less than `cover_m` along the buried run, or under a road less than `max(cover_m, rules.road_cover_m)`. The finding gives the file `layout/plant-model.yaml`, the ids `[pipe, road]`, a `box`, `measured` = cover, and a hint pointing to `piping/routing.yaml`. Keys are `<pipe>+<road>` / `<pipe>`. Vertical runs (risers through grade) are left out. `road_cover_m` defaults to **1.2 m, marked ASSUMED** and configurable in `rules:` (see Sources). The rule is added to the default `clashes` rules of the layout gates, so a buried declaration does not take a road crossing out of the gate. |
| 2. Clash checks treat buried parts sensibly against above-grade objects | A buried run is not compared with steel, equipment parts, access envelopes or zone volumes that stand wholly above grade. A steel member is judged by its axis, so a column on grade whose capsule ends 0.15 m below grade no longer clashes. A footing below grade still clashes (tested). Ladder clearance skips buried runs. Buried level runs get no `free-span` or `support-missing` finding. Pipe-to-pipe clashes are unchanged (buried against buried is real). |
| 2. The MTO can tell buried pipe | Pipe rows split: the length in the ground is a row with `group: buried` (e.g. `pipe DN1400 bare buried`). A riser counts up to where its top leaves the ground. |
| 3. Without the field, behaviour is unchanged (golden files unchanged) | The field defaults to absent and nothing is emitted. All existing tests and goldens pass unchanged. On ammonia-1 without the field, rebuilding with this branch changed only the generator hash in the model's provenance, and the findings were identical (below). |
| Schema, findings, tests (before/after fixture), docs, skill, manifest, ADR | `tests/test_layout_buried.py` has 9 tests, each fixture checked before and after setting `buried`. Docs updated: `docs/framework/layout-model.md`, `docs/framework/mto.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, CHANGELOG, `pipe-routing` skill. I left `layout-yaml` alone because routing intent is not in its scope. I reran `scripts/build_skill_manifest.py` and regenerated `tests/data/init-manifest.txt`. New ADR **0036** (origin/main merged just before; 0036 was free). |

## Real case: ammonia-1 (process-library `nh3-run-final`, copied to `build/`, not committed there)

I added `buried: {basis: D-038}` to the 38 CWS/CWR entries of `piping/routing.yaml`, removed the owner's 4 `layout-headroom` acceptances from `checks/checks.yaml`, and ran this branch's `cheme layout build` and `cheme check --stage detail`.

| | before (input as tagged, rebuilt with this branch) | after (`buried` declared) |
|---|---|---|
| `cheme.layout-headroom` | 4 (CWS-1144/CWR-1145 S2 × R-5, S8 × R-6, "-3.71 m clear") | **0** |
| `cheme.layout-buried-cover` | – | **0** (headers: 2.29 m cover under R-5/R-6, ≥ 1.2 m) |
| `cheme.layout-support-missing` (info) | 107 | 64 (43 buried CW runs gone) |
| every other rule | same counts | same counts |
| gate `layout-3d` | FAIL: 4 headroom not accepted | **ok** |
| gate `layout-detail` | FAIL: 4 headroom not accepted | **ok** |
| MTO | DN 1400 bare 490 m | `pipe DN1400 bare buried` 490 m. Branches split, e.g. DN 700: 171 m above grade + 209 m buried |

One CW support-missing remains: `P-114/Line_CWS1063_S1` (DN 400). The routed branch rises to +0.2 m (centreline) over 8.5 m between the header tees, so that run really is above grade, and the rules treat it as such. The plant can fix it by pinning the branch below grade. Without the owner's acceptances, the two layout gates now pass on the rules alone.

## Sources and tolerances

- `road_cover_m` 1.2 m is **ASSUMED**. Secondary sources cite 1.2 m (4 ft) from the road surface to the top of an uncased carrier pipe after API RP 1102: [PPNS journal](https://journal.ppns.ac.id/index.php/CPEAA/article/view/3445), [Technical Toolboxes API 1102 highway crossing](https://help.technicaltoolboxes.com/?p=1956), [Arkansas rule 91-301](https://www.state-rules.com/arkansas/car/91-301/) (48 in from ditch flow line / 60 in from surface). (Reviewer: the Technical Toolboxes page was verified, "4ft <= H <= 10 ft for highways (API 1102)", and is now cited in the docs and the ADR; the PPNS and Arkansas pages could not be retrieved (403) and are not cited in the repository.) I could not check the value against the API standard's text, so it is not presented as the standard's value. The site's or road authority's rule replaces it in `rules.road_cover_m`, or per line in `buried.cover_m`.
- Tolerances: a run is buried when top ≤ grade + 1 mm (`TOUCH`). A solid is above grade when its bottom (a member's axis end) is ≥ grade − 1 mm. Cover findings fire when the shortfall is > 1 mm. In the MTO a top within 1 mm above grade still counts as in the ground.

## Commands run

- `uv run ruff format && uv run ruff check`: clean
- `uv run pytest -n 2 -q`: 3893 passed, 128 skipped
- `uv run python scripts/build_skill_manifest.py`; `uv run python tests/test_init_golden.py > tests/data/init-manifest.txt`
- On the scratch copy: `cheme layout build`, `cheme check --stage detail`, `cheme assess mto --write` (before/after above)

Closes #70

Part of #165: the filter-dryer and NBS lesson L-3. The batch distillation and solvent swap, the precipitation from a mixed liquor and L-5 are in the other #165 PRs (ADRs 0054-0056).

## What it adds
- **`dryer:` on a block or step** (`domains/process/dryer.py`). It takes one wet-cake inlet and has `outlets: {product, vapour}`.
  - The `volatiles` dry down to a `residual_moisture`, given as `mass_fraction` or `per_kg_solid`.
  - The solid, and whatever the cake liquid held dissolved, stays in the product.
  - `process propagate` writes both outlets. The model basis is `residual-moisture` (specified). The rules are `cheme.process-dryer`.
- **Energy** (`dryer.energy`): `Q = (m cp (T - T_in) + sum W_i lambda_i + C_v (T - T_in) / h_batch) / eta`.
  - A latent heat that is not declared comes from the component's critical constants by Pitzer's corresponding states (Poling et al. 2001, eq. 7-9.4).
  - The vessel term is counted per batch of `process/recipe.yaml`.
  - `process crystallizers` reports dryers too, and compares the duty with the heating stream at `energy.port`.
- **Recipe**:
  - `dry` with `from:` a dryer: one batch's vapour over `drying_rate` (kg/(m2 h)) times the vessel's heated area, or the dryer's `drying_time`. The heated area is `vessel.heated_area`, else the jacket's area, else the shell and bottom the cake wets.
  - `filter` with `from:` a `solid_separation:` that gives `filtration:`: Ruth's constant-pressure time. There is no filtration time without a specific cake resistance.
  - `units: [steps]` instead of `unit:` puts several steps in one vessel (filter, wash, re-filter, dry), and the occupancy is counted once. A step in two vessels is `cheme.recipe-reference`.
  - A filter-dryer's vessel is sized from the dryer's wet cake over its `cake_density` (R10, as in ADR 0052).
- **Unchanged behaviour.** `dryer`, `filtration`, `units` and `heated_area` are left out of model dumps when absent (`exclude_if`). Plain batches, semi-batches, crystallizers, filters and recipes behave and fingerprint as before.
- **PharmaPy** was reviewed and not adopted: Assimulo cannot be installed on Python 3.12+ with uv, and PharmaPy has no agitated or vacuum filter-dryer. The ADR records this and cites its paper as literature only. No code was copied.

## Docs
ADR 0057 (with its mkdocs nav entry and README row), a REFERENCE.md entry, CHANGELOG under Unreleased/Added, the `separation-method-selection` skill (its coverage row for Drying is now `dryer`, tested) and `process-design`, and the maturity table. The skill manifest and init manifest are regenerated, the example BFD/PFD sheets rebuilt (the generator's hash changed), and only `yaml-flowsheet.json` of the viewer fixtures is regenerated.

## Tests
`tests/test_dryer.py` (9 tests):
- the dryer's mass and energy balance against a hand calculation;
- propagate filling the outlets, with the F1, D1 and ISO balances ok;
- the duty terms and the heating-stream comparison;
- Pitzer against measured heats of vaporization of water and benzene;
- the drying time as rate x area and the vessel sized from the cake;
- the Ruth filtration time against its closed form;
- a recipe unit over two steps with its occupancy counted once;
- the reference errors;
- model dumps without the new fields.

`uv run pytest -n auto`: 4259 passed, 131 skipped. `ruff format`/`ruff check` are clean, and `mkdocs build --strict` passes.

## Limits
- The residual moisture and the drying rate are specified, not predicted. There is no falling-rate period, critical moisture or sorption isotherm.
- Several volatiles leave in their inlet ratio.
- The boiling point under vacuum, the condenser and the agitator or vacuum-pump power are not modelled.
- The cake is incompressible (constant alpha).
- The wash is still a user-chosen mixer plus filter (no washing efficiency).
- Two unit procedures that both name the same single `unit:` still do not add their occupancies (ADR 0051).

Do not merge before review.

**P1-high.** Implementation child of #220 (equipment sizing, rating and integrated hydraulic design). Build reusable engineering calculations, connected to plant artifacts and operating cases.

## Scope

- Define a versioned scenario record with protected equipment, initiating condition, safeguards assumptions, relieving state and load basis.
- Deliver in bounded increments: first a well-defined nonreactive single-phase scenario and device-sizing method; add other cases only with qualified load models.

- Declare applicable standard/method editions, coefficients, units, backpressure basis and device limitations.

Independent load and sizing benchmarks; absent scenario/property/coefficient data blocks a complete result; governing scenario selection is traceable; generic computed area never implies a certified device or complete protection study.

hits.body:
Fixes the 1 mm offset between a branch and its tee on a battery-limit header (regression of #72, v1.2.0).

## Root cause

`Router._plan` split the header's route in steps (`split_at(rest, cut - done)`, each on the simplified remainder) but gave the branch a tee point computed separately on the whole route (`point_at(route, cut)`). The two points differ by float rounding error. When the model is written to the millimetre, they can round to different values. In ammonia-1's CWS-1144 the header piece ended at x `219.65249999999997` and the tee was at `219.6525`, so they were written as 219.652 and 219.653. The branch then did not end on its header's run, and the clash rule's tee exemption (`< 1e-3` from the run) did not apply. `_cuts` itself (the arc lengths) was correct; only the two separate evaluations of the same cut disagreed.

## Fix

`geometry3d.split_at_many` cuts the route in one pass. It returns each cut point once: as the end of one piece, the start of the next, and the junction point the branch starts from. If a branch was routed first, its pinned junction point is used as the cut point when it is within 1 µm of the cut. No clash tolerance is changed.

## Acceptance checks

- **Branch starts exactly at its tee on the header**: done. One shared coordinate per tee, rounded once.
- **A branch leaving its own header at the tee is not a clash**: done. The tee exemption now applies because the points are equal.
- **Root cause fixed where it is, not by widening a tolerance**: done (above).
- **Behaviour elsewhere unchanged**: the full suite passes with no golden file changed. `viewer/tests/fixtures/layout-mep.json` changes only its `generator_sha256` (routing.py changed), as in 4e68f4e. No golden file had the defect.
- **Regression test**: `tests/test_layout_bl_headers.py::test_each_branch_starts_exactly_where_its_header_is_cut_for_the_tee`. It routes a BL-to-BL header whose limits sit on the rack centreline, off its lane (a jog), with four branches at non-round x (37.0525, 39.0525, 41.0525, 58.2175). It asserts header end == next piece start == branch start, both before and after the model's 3-decimal rounding, and no `cheme.layout-clash-pipe` from `model_rules`. On the old routing code it fails at T1 (`39.05250000000001 != 39.052499999999995`, written 39.053 against 39.052). `test_split_at_many_shares_each_cut_point` covers the helper on ammonia-1's route and cuts.
- **CHANGELOG** under Unreleased, Fixed: done.

## Real case: ammonia-1 (stage/detail-core120), scratch copy, not committed there

I copied `processes/ammonia-1` into `build/` of this worktree and ran `cheme layout build` and `cheme check` with main (before) and with this branch (after).

- **Before**: `layout build` gave "unchanged layout/plant-model.yaml": main reproduces the committed model. It reports 3 `layout-clash-pipe` at 0.00 m: CWS-1052/CWS1144_S2, CWS-1063/CWS1144_S3, CWS-1074/CWS1144_S4. `layout-3d` and `layout-detail` FAIL on them.
- **After**: 0 `layout-clash-pipe`. `layout-3d` and `layout-detail` are ok. Every other build finding is identical.
- **Model diff**: only the 4 CWS-1144 header points at T1052/T1063/T1074 move from x .652 to .653 (S2 end, S3, S4, S5 start), now equal to the branch starts, plus `generator_sha256`/`output_sha256`. Pipe counts, routed segments (250/260) and everything else are unchanged.
- **Side effect in the plant**: `lifting-study` reports stale because `layout/lifting-study.md` records the model's `output_sha256`. `cheme layout lifting --write` changes only that hash line. The plant has to rebuild its model and rerun that command after upgrading.
- Other gate failures in the scratch copy (`design-review`, `layout-review`: reviewed commits are not in the scratch repository's fresh git history; `datasheets`) are the same before and after.

## Commands run

- `uv run ruff format && uv run ruff check`
- `uv run pytest -n 2`: 3910 passed, 128 skipped
- `uv run python viewer/scripts/regen-fixtures.py`: only `layout-mep.json`'s generator hash kept. `reactions-shift.json` differed in last-digit floats from this macOS/Python 3.15 environment, which is unrelated to this change, so I did not commit it. The viewer CI on Linux is the authority.

Closes #95

## Problem
Core and DEXPI records need explicit, reviewable mappings to standard asset classifications and property definitions for interoperability. Similar labels alone do not establish semantic equivalence, and an unversioned mapping can silently change meaning.

## Scope
Bounded implementation slice of #242 and preparation for #252; support #249 without replacing DEXPI or the HAZOP schema.

- Select and pin an official CFIHOS release and reference-data source; record source URL, checksum, version and applicable reuse terms.
- Start with vessels, relief devices, isolation/control valves and instruments. Define an explicit coverage matrix rather than claiming full CFIHOS support.
- Map selected existing DEXPI/core classes and properties to verified CFIHOS identifiers.
- Record mapping direction and relation: exact, broader, narrower, related or unresolved, with rationale, provenance and review status.
- Preserve class identity separately from project object identity; use the lifecycle/identity work in #268.
- Handle units, value types, enumerations and lifecycle context explicitly. Keep unmatched properties and original identifiers without silent loss.
- Use ISO 15926 reference identifiers where directly supported by authoritative mappings; do not invent equivalence or require wholesale ontology adoption.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every mapped identifier is verified against the pinned reference-data package, with deterministic offline lookup.
- [ ] A reviewed mapping fixture covers each selected equipment family and distinguishes exact from partial mappings.
- [ ] Unsupported, ambiguous and deprecated terms are surfaced; missing mappings never become guessed classifications.
- [ ] A representative package round-trip preserves identity, units, provenance, lifecycle status and unmapped data, or explicitly reports unavoidable losses.
- [ ] Changing the mapping release produces a reviewable semantic diff and invalidates dependent interpretations when needed.
- [ ] Document coverage, mapping format, import/export adapter boundaries and tests.
- [ ] Keep the pilot usable without a network lookup or external graph database at runtime.

## References and boundary
Use official CFIHOS resources: https://www.jip36-cfihos.org/cfihos-standards/
This issue establishes a limited mapping capability, not full CFIHOS conformance or a complete handover implementation. Reuse existing models and adapters.

The router now routes a line with battery limits at both ends. In ammonia-1 these are the cooling-water headers from the battery limit to their users' dead end along PR-1. Before, such a line stayed unrouted ("battery limit: no other end to start from"), and every branch waited for a tee that no route reached. That is why the run's agent pinned the header routes by hand.

## What changed
- `routing.py` `Router._limits`: a chain whose two ends are both battery limits gets both ends placed together.
  - The matching `battery_limits` rules each place one end, in file order. A second matching rule used to be ignored, so this only matters for such lines.
  - An end no rule places goes to the far end of a rack. The rack is the line's `rack` intent, else the rule's rack, else the rack nearest the rule point or the line's branches, else the longest rack.
  - Rack ends sit on the line's tier (`tier` intent or `tiers` rule) or at its `elevation` intent.
  - The line runs the way its tees come, so the branches tee off in their order. Without this, a rule naming the *east* end bunched all of the return header's tees at its west end.
  - When it still cannot place the line, the line stays unrouted with the reason `battery limits at both ends (<from> and <to>): ...`. The cases are: no rack to run along, a `rack` intent that is not a rack, a rule rack that is missing, or both ends at the same point.
- Lines with at most one battery limit take the old code path unchanged.
- Docs: module text, `docs/framework/layout-model.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, the `pipe-routing` skill (rules and unrouted reasons) and the CHANGELOG. I reran `scripts/build_skill_manifest.py` and regenerated `tests/data/init-manifest.txt`.
- No ADR: no public file format or schema changes. The `routing.yaml` schema is unchanged; for these lines a second matching rule is now used, where it used to be ignored. Unrouted reasons are free text in the model, as before.

## Acceptance checks
| Check | Done |
|---|---|
| Routes a BL-to-BL line along the rack/tier its intent names, or the default | yes. Tests: default rack and tier, `rack`+`tier` intent, `elevation` intent, nearest rack to the branches |
| Branches and tees resolved as for other lines | yes. Tees are placed where the branches go (`_cuts`), and each branch runs from its tee to its user. Test with a header and two branches, including one where the rule names the far end |
| Clear finding naming why when it still cannot | yes. Parametrised test over the four refusal reasons; the branches then report the tee no route reaches |
| Pinned routes stay pinned and win | yes. Test with a pinned middle segment. On ammonia-1 with the committed (pinned) inputs, the model is byte-identical apart from `provenance.generator_sha256` (the hash of the router source) |
| Without such lines behaviour unchanged (golden files unchanged) | yes. No golden or test-data change except the init manifest (skill hash). Full suite passes |
| Tests, docs, bundled skill `pipe-routing`, manifest regenerated | yes |

## Real case: ammonia-1 (process-library `nh3-run-final`), scratch copy under `build/`, nothing committed there
Run with this branch's `uv run cheme layout build` and `cheme check`. In every run the 10 unrouted segments are the skipped furnace ducts.

| Inputs | Routed | CW headers | `layout-clash-pipe` | `cheme check` layout gates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| As committed (headers pinned, hand routes buried at -3.0 m) | 248/258 | hand: CWS-1144 275 m, CWR-1145 215 m | 0 | – |
| Headers unpinned, **old router** | 192/258 (66 unrouted: 20 header segments, 36 branch segments waiting for tees) | unrouted | 0 | `layout-detail` FAIL: 20 lines neither routed nor skipped |
| V1: headers unpinned, **this branch** | 248/258 | on PR-1, lowest tier (6.0 m, DN 1400), from one PR-1 end to the other: 320 m + 320 m | 9 | `layout-3d`, `layout-detail` FAIL: 9 clash-pipe, 2 headroom not accepted |
| V2: as V1 + `{line: CWS-1144/CWR-1145, elevation: -3.0}` (the hand design's depth) | 248/258 | buried at -3.0 m along PR-1's line: CWS 324 m, CWR 320 m | 2 | `layout-3d`, `layout-detail` FAIL: 2 clash-pipe |
| V3: as V2 + a second `battery_limits` point rule per header at its dead end | 248/258 | CWS 279 m, CWR 215 m (hand: 275 m, 215 m) | 5 | – |

**Comparison with the hand-written routes**
- **Length.** Without a second rule, the dead end ("CW users") is treated as a battery limit at the far PR-1 end. So V1/V2 come out 45 m (supply) and 105 m (return) longer than the hand routes. With a point rule for the dead end (V3), the return is exactly the hand length and the supply is 4 m longer: it steps 2 m sideways to clear the return and back.
- **Tees.** Supply tees at x 127, 220, 222, 224, 242, 244, 246, 295, 297; the hand routes have them at 127, 205, 207.5, 210, 212.5, 215, 232, 289, 292. The router puts each tee where the branch's user is. The hand design puts them where the branches' via points meet the header.
- **V1 clashes** (headers on the rack):
  - 3 are CWR-1145 S8 against PG-1081, PG-1082 and BW-1100.
  - 1 is CWS-1085 between its own P-107 and P-114 segments.
  - 5 are between other lines pushed out of their lanes by the two DN 1400 headers on PR-1's lowest tier: NG-1001/FG-1010, SM-1005/BW-1025, BW-1024/BW-1025, BW-1037/SM-1140, PC-1048/SM-1038.
  - Other finding counts: free-span 73→83, support-missing 107→100, headroom 4→2, lifting 8→10, `rack+direct` fallbacks 1→4.
- **V2 clashes** (buried): only the 2 branch clashes (CWS-1085 between its two sheets' segments, CWS-1041/CWR-1042). All other finding counts equal the pinned baseline, except support-missing 107→109.
- **Why the remaining clashes are in the plant's inputs.** The branches' `via`/`elevation` intents were written for the hand tee positions (and for -1.8 m over buried headers). They still aim there when the router puts the tees elsewhere. Fixing them is plant work and is not done here.
- **Other FAILs** are the same in every run and unrelated: design/layout review (the scratch repo has no history, so `reviewed_commit` is not a commit), electrical tray fill, datasheets. `mto` and `lifting-study` go stale after any model change.

**Seen, not changed** (already on main, not this issue): on any rack line with tees, the segments between two tees have no `racks`/`tier` in the model (e.g. FLR-1146 S3/S5 on main), because `_plan` only marks segments that touch a lane end.

## Commands run
- `uv run ruff format && uv run ruff check`
- `uv run pytest -n 2`: 3893 passed, 128 skipped
- `uv run pytest -n 2 tests/test_layout_bl_headers.py`: 9 passed. 8 of them fail on main's router; the pin test passes there too, by design.
- `uv run python scripts/build_skill_manifest.py`, `uv run python tests/test_init_golden.py > tests/data/init-manifest.txt`
- On the scratch copy: `cheme layout build`, `cheme layout build --check`, `cheme check` for each row above

Closes #72

Found by benzyl-chloroformate-1 (process-library#384), sodium-azide-1 (#386), methylmagnesium-bromide-1 (#383) and n-bromosuccinimide-1 (#382).

## The gap
Only `dryer:` compares its energy stream with its model (`cheme.process-dryer-duty`). The other batch models neither write nor check the duty on their energy port:
- batch and semi-batch reactors (the year-average cooling duty, the jacket's peak);
- `still:` (boil-up energy);
- `crystallizer:` (with spectators);
- conversion steps.

So every entry types the duties in by hand. They do not go stale when the model changes, and `cheme process reactors` shows `?` for the duty.

## Wanted
- An energy `port:` on each of these models.
- `propagate --fill` writes the year-average duty there (per batch times batches per hour), with its fingerprint.
- `validate` compares a given duty with the model's value, as `cheme.process-dryer-duty` does.
